function.arguments: {"finding": "Female patients have higher baseline severity than males in the control arm, but lower in the treatment arm. This imbalance is not random: clinicians assigned the treatment to sicker patients, especially males, who are more likely to have severe disease. As a result, the treatment arm contains more severe cases, which respond worse regardless of treatment. However, within each severity stratum, males respond better than females. The observed higher response rate in females is due to a confounding: females are less likely to be assigned to the treatment arm (which is worse for severe cases), so they are over-represented in the better-performing control arm.", "implication": "The question assumes that the observed difference in response rates by sex is due to biological sex, but it is actually confounded by severity and non-random treatment assignment. function.name: note_finding
